summary.intent: Evaluate all open PRs in orin-dx/callisto across Rust best practices, repo conventions, performance, security, maintainability and architecture; then ensure the Codex and Entire config is tracked in the repo via a PR so Entire detects the Codex hooks.
summary.outcome: Reviewed seven open PRs, finding two high-severity blockers (#195 Cargo target dependency collapse, #188 release PR with no CI checks) and one low (#192). Prepared branch chore/track-codex-entire-config un-ignoring .codex/hooks.json, got user approval, and began committing/pushing; final PR creation was not confirmed in the transcript.

repo: Entire detects Codex via .codex/hooks.json, not .entire/settings.json; .gitignore previously excluded all of .codex/, so hooks.json was untracked.
The .entire/settings.json and .entire/.gitignore are already tracked on main.
The .codex/agents/bug-hunter.toml contains a machine-specific path and is intentionally kept ignored.
Codex users must review project hooks with /hooks on each fresh checkout before they run.
The repo CI workflow (.github/workflows/callisto-ci.yml) covers PRs to main, but generated release PR #188 had no check run attached and was UNSTABLE.
The repo has a courier:pr skill requiring exact PR details to be shown and explicit user confirmation before pushing or opening a PR.
Open PRs are stacked: #196 on #195, and #193 on #190; #188 is a generated release PR publishing 0.10.1.

code.finding: Dependency iterator reports only the first declaration per (kind, name), collapsing top-level and target-specific dependencies that share a local key.
Rewrite path changes every declaration with the same (kind, name) key, so bumping one can rewrite another target's differing pin; workspace inheritance is tracked by the same coarse key.
New constructor in #192 validates only package_members(), so a group containing only a platform manifest looks empty even though config resolution accepts it.
Ignore rule narrowed so .codex/hooks.json is tracked while other local Codex files stay ignored.

workflow: GitHub access failed in the sandbox, so review fell back to read-only routes and local PR refs.
Prepare config changes on an isolated branch based on current origin/main rather than the working checkout.
Validate config-only changes with JSON parsing and git diff --check, and verify the tool (Entire) recognizes the result.
Review stacked PRs against their actual bases, not main.

friction: GitHub access failed in the sandbox, forcing fallback to read-only routes and local PR refs.
macOS tests for #195 and #196 were still running at review time, so CI results were incomplete.
Local Cargo tests were not run against PR heads, limiting the review to diff and execution-path analysis.
open_items: Request changes on #195: keep target dependency declarations distinct through graph construction and rewriting, and add tests for differing aliases, constraints and inheritance.
Run required CI validation on the exact head commit of release PR #188 before merging.
Fix #192 constructor to validate all members (including platform manifests) while checking package ownership separately.
Confirm the config PR for chore/track-codex-entire-config was actually pushed and opened.
No review comments were posted to the PRs.
